t:
Title VI of the Rural Electrification Act of 1936 (7 U.S.C. 950bb et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:
“SEC. 602. NATIONAL CENTER FOR RURAL TELECOMMUNICATIONS ASSESSMENT.“(a) Designation of Center.—The Secretary shall designate an entity to serve as the National Center for Rural Telecommunications Assessment (referred to in this section as the ‘Center’).“(b) Criteria.—In designating the Center under subsection (a), the Secretary shall take into consideration the following criteria:“(1) The Center shall be an entity that demonstrates to the Secretary—“(A) a focus on rural policy research; and“(B) a minimum of 5 years of experience relating to rural telecommunications research and assessment.“(2) The Center shall be capable of assessing broadband services in rural areas.“(3) The Center shall have significant experience involving other rural economic development centers and organizations with respect to the assessment of rural policies and the formulation of policy solutions at the Federal, State, and local levels.“(c) Board of Directors.—The Center shall be managed by a board of directors, which shall be responsible for the duties of the Center described in subsection (d).“(d) Duties.—The Center shall—“(1) assess the effectiveness of programs carried out under this title in increasing broadband penetration and purchase in rural areas, especially in rural communities identified by the Secretary as having no broadband service before the provision of a loan or loan guarantee under this title;“(2) work with existing rural development centers selected by the Center to identify policies and initiatives at the Federal, State, and local levels that have increased broadband penetration and purchase in rural areas and provide recommendations to Federal, State, and local policymakers on effective strategies to bring affordable broadband services to residents of rural areas, particularly residents located outside of the municipal boundaries of a rural city or town; and“(3) develop and publish reports describing the activities carried out by the Center under this section.“(e) Reporting Requirements.—Not later than December 1 of each applicable fiscal year, the board of directors of the Center shall submit to Congress and the Secretary a report describing the activities carried out by the Center during the preceding fiscal year and the results of any research conducted by the Center during that fiscal year, including—“(1) an assessment of each program carried out under this title; and“(2) an assessment of the effects of the policy initiatives identified under subsection (d)(2).“(f) Authorization of Appropriations.—There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $1,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2012.”
.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a non-federal Center giving recommendations to federal policymakers works like an outside advisory body. But the Center is a designated research entity that assesses programs and publishes reports; no federal decision is conditioned on consulting it, and no comment period, hearing, rulemaking or right to sue is created. Its reports to Congress and the Secretary are research outputs rather than outside involvement in a specific federal decision, and the designation itself resembles a grant or contract selection. This is a close call, since the recommendations do cross the federal boundary.
fable.s: provide recommendations to Federal, State, and local policymakers on effective strategies to bring affordable broadband services to residents of rural areas

opus.w: The Secretary designates a non-federal research entity with its own board of directors. That entity assesses federal programs and gives recommendations to federal policymakers, so outside experts are feeding advice into federal policy, much like the advisory commissions in Examples 8 and 12. The opposite reading treats this as just a report to Congress or a study, as in Example 3. That reading misses that the Center's own policy recommendations go directly to federal decision-makers, which brings outsiders into federal decisions.
opus.s: work with existing rural development centers selected by the Center to identify policies and initiatives at the Federal, State, and local levels that have increased broadband penetration and purchase in rural areas and provide recommendations to Federal, State, and local policymakers on effective strategies to bring affordable broadband services to residents of rural areas
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** This looks like a "No," much like Example 3. The Center mainly runs studies and sends reports to Congress, and reports to Congress stay inside the federal government. It could also be read as the Secretary simply picking a funding recipient, which is like awarding a grant.

**Why I chose "Yes" anyway:** The Center is an outside entity. It must have a focus on rural policy research and 5 years of experience, which points to a university or research center rather than a federal agency. It is run by its own board of directors. Its job is not just to study but to give recommendations to federal policymakers, which is like the outside expert committees in Examples 8 and 12. Example 3 differs because there outside experts only helped write the government's own study. Here, the outside body advises decision-makers directly. This is a close call.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes a Center that reports to Congress and the Secretary. Congress and the Secretary are inside the federal government. The Center is designated to perform assessments and provide recommendations, but the statute does not require the Secretary to consult with the Center or any outside party before making a decision. The reporting requirement is a one-way flow of information from the Center to the government, not a participatory process involving outside parties in the decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: (e) Reporting Requirements.—Not later than December 1 of each applicable fiscal year, the board of directors of the Center shall submit to Congress and the Secretary a report describing the activities carried out the Center during the preceding fiscal year and the results of any research conducted by the Center during that fiscal year
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Center" is an outside entity (likely a non-profit or university) and that its board of directors provides advice to the government, thus constituting participation. However, the statute does not require the Secretary to consult with the Center before making decisions; rather, the Secretary designates the Center to perform assessments and report findings. The Center's role is to provide data and recommendations, but there is no mandatory consultation or coordination with outside parties *before* a federal decision is made. The reporting is to Congress (inside government) and the Secretary (inside government). The "participation" definition requires consultation or coordination *before* a decision, or an advisory board with non-federal members that influences a decision. Here, the Center is a designated entity performing a specific task, not a participatory body in the decision-making process itself. Furthermore, the board of directors manages the Center, not the federal agency.
